newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Kersaf says no decision yet on Interleisure.
newsitem.headline: Kersaf says no decision yet on Interleisure.

text.p: South African investment group, Kersaf Ltd, said on Friday it was still evaluating its options with regards to the future of its stake in entertainment firm, Interleisure Ltd.

Rumours circulated on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) on Friday that Interleisure was poised to be sold off to media group Sasani Ltd SSAJ.J. Sasani shares jumped to a high of 148 cents, a rise of 12 percent in brisk trade of almost two million shares by 1050 GMT.
But Kersaf chairman Buddy Hawton, who is also chairman of Interleisure, told Reuters no decision on Interleisure had yet been made.
"We are looking into the future holding and direction of Interleisure in the light of the Servgro unbundling...," Hawton told Reuters.
"But as far as we are concerned we are still evaulating our alternatives," he said.
Hawton said discussions had been held with a number of parties, including Sasani, but no decision had yet been made.
Sasani could not be reached for comment.
Speculation surrounding the sale of Interleisure comes amid the unbundling of Servgro International, which together with Kersaf jointly owns Interleisure.

The industrial conglomerate last week said that the second phase of the unbundling, which will result in the distribution of its cash resources and any realisation proceeds of its remaining assets and/or the distribution of shares in its remaining assets, was unlikely to be announced before June 30.
Sasani is still under a cautionary announcement published on April 11 in which it said it was still in talks on acquisitions which could impact on its share price.
Interleisure is a stakeholder in Sasani, which also has as stakeholders video business Video Lab and black empowerment group Msomi Ventures.
Other than Interleisure, Servgro's assets include Teljoy Holdings Ltd, Fedics Group (Pty) Ltd and Interpark (Pty) Ltd.
Following its unbundling Servgro may liquidate and delist.
